title: SEC-000001: Authenticated and confidential transport for externally reachable network services
statement: The BMS master software shall not service any externally reachable network session until the peer has been authenticated by a cryptographically sound mechanism, and shall protect the confidentiality and integrity of all session data after authentication.
rationale: A network service that accepts an unauthenticated peer is exposed to anyone who can route a packet to its interface, and every later control in the security concept is then built on an unauthenticated channel. The requirement is written ahead of the hypothetical project's planned diagnostic and configuration service (TARA threat THR-007) as well as the service that exists today, so that the higher-consequence service is not designed without authentication. confidentiality is required in addition to authentication because a reflecting service on a fixed interface is usable by a third party as a stable traffic-reflection endpoint even when it grants the peer no access to internal data (TARA threat THR-002).

acceptance_criteria.measure: TCP connections completed against the service port from a peer that fails authentication, counted over a 24 h window
Time from TCP handshake completion to first application data accepted from the peer
Plaintext bytes of application payload recoverable from a captured session by a passive observer on the segment
Payload bytes altered in transit that are accepted by the receiver
Diagnosis entries raised per failed authentication attempt

safety_allocation.mitigation: Security mitigation for the freedom-from-interference assumption of the safety requirements. This requirement is classified as a security requirement, not an ASIL allocation; asil is recorded as not_applicable because ISO 26262 does not allocate ASIL to a security requirement. It is traced to FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 because a compromised communication path can undermine the assurance of the requirements derived from that goal.

standards_mappings.reference: Clause 8.5 (security requirements) derived from the Clause 15 mitigation concept; communication protection concept per Clause 10
standards_mappings.rationale: Named for traceability of intent only. No ISO/SAE 21434 work product exists in this corpus, clause conformance is not claimed, and the mapping has not been reviewed by any authority.
The hypothetical project has no communication protection concept. The gap is deliberate and is what this requirement is intended to close.

standards_mappings.reference: Part 4, Clause 7 (technical safety requirements, freedom from interference)
standards_mappings.rationale: Only the identification of the communication path as an interference vector is mapped. The freedom-from-interference analysis itself is not part of this corpus.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Forward-engineered security requirement 'authenticated-transport-network-service' for the synthetic_reference project. Derived from threat analysis FB2-SAF-TAR-000001.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the asil_justification that the requirement applicability validator requires and did not find: this record marks safety_allocation.asil as not_applicable, which requirement.schema.json enumerates as the value for a requirement to which no ASIL determination applies, and the rule requires a recorded reason for that marking. The reason had been present only inside safety_allocation.mitigation and safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref, which are required on every requirement whatever its marking and are therefore populated identically on the ASIL_D records; they cannot serve as a justification specific to this marking. The new field states the reason on its own, names what the safety_goal_ref trace does and does not carry, and records the open items where the marking depends on something not yet established. The asil value, the statement, the mitigation, the safety_goal_ref and the revision-relevant content of the record are unchanged. Remediation of the requirement applicability validator finding raised by finding FB2-REV-FND-000032. Nothing in this field asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

real_source_presence: Control ABSENT. The real foxBMS 2 master's only network service is a plain-TCP echo server: src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:255 creates an AF_INET/SOCK_STREAM/IPPROTO_TCP socket, :276-281 binds it, :288 calls FreeRTOS_accept, and the accepted socket is handed to a task at :292 with no credential exchange, no peer-address check and no cryptographic handshake. The peer address is captured by accept as an output parameter and never inspected, and the endpoint parameter is explicitly discarded at :248. No TLS or equivalent cryptographic library is present in the master communication stack. Anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000057.
real_source_control_status_note: The control this requirement specifies is NOT present in the real foxBMS 2 source at commit 308028fb.

asil_justification.scope_of_this_classification: This field records why safety_allocation.asil is not_applicable on this requirement. It is a statement about this record's own allocation bookkeeping inside a fictional reference project. It is not a determination about the real foxBMS 2 product, which has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment, and it is not evidence about that product's security architecture.
asil_justification.reason: This requirement is classified 'security' and it specifies an authenticated transport service. ISO 26262 allocates an ASIL to a safety requirement derived from a hazard analysis and risk assessment; it does not allocate an ASIL to a security requirement, which is why the field carries the schema's own enumerated value not_applicable rather than a class. The classification field on this record and the value in safety_allocation.asil therefore agree, and the marking is a faithful report of what this requirement is rather than a decision taken to avoid a classification.
asil_justification.safety_goal_ref_meaning: The safety_goal_ref on this record is FB2-SAF-SGO-000001. That reference is a trace and not an allocation: a compromised communication path can undermine the assurance of the requirements derived from that goal, which is why the link exists. No ASIL flows down this reference and none is implied by it.
what_this_does_not_assert: It does not assert conformity with ISO 26262, and it is not a certification, a type approval, or evidence of one. Nothing in this field was audited to produce it.

It does not assert human approval. human_approval_status on this record is pending, production_authorized is false and product_verification_credit is false, and no functional-safety expert has confirmed any of it.
It does not establish that any ASIL was correctly assigned to any safety requirement in this corpus. It explains only why this requirement is not itself an ASIL-allocated item.
It does not assert tool qualification. No tool used anywhere in this corpus has been qualified for a safety purpose.
It does not assert an ASPICE capability level for anything.
